root_cause.text: gmap_helper_zap_one_page() in the s390 gmap/KVM memory management path unconditionally cleared swap PTEs and softleaf entries without validating the PGSTE guest-page state, so pages still marked as in-use or zero-tracked by the guest could be wrongly discarded and cause guest memory corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new `pgstev = pgste_val(pgste);` check and only executes `ptep_zap_softleaf_entry(mm, softleaf_from_pte(*ptep));` and `pte_clear(mm, vmaddr, ptep);` when `(pgstev & _PGSTE_GPS_USAGE_MASK) == _PGSTE_GPS_USAGE_UNUSED || (pgstev & _PGSTE_GPS_ZERO)`, while the CVE/commit message explicitly says “A few checks were missing in gmap_helper_zap_one_page(), which can lead to memory corruption in the guest.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local pgstev variable to gmap_helper_zap_one_page() to support upcoming PGSTE-related logic.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration, "unsigned long pgstev;", was added inside gmap_helper_zap_one_page() alongside the existing local variables.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this introduces storage for an unsigned long value within the function, likely to hold PGSTE-related state for later use in the function body; in the shown hunk alone, it does not change behavior except enabling subsequent code to compile or use that value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Only clear swapped PTEs and remove their softleaf entries when PGSTE state marks them unused or zero, avoiding incorrect zapping of active entries.
intent_record.what: Inside the pte_swap(*ptep) branch of gmap_helper_zap_one_page(), a new local value assignment `pgstev = pgste_val(pgste);` was added after acquiring the PGSTE lock, and the previously unconditional calls to `ptep_zap_softleaf_entry(mm, softleaf_from_pte(*ptep));` and `pte_clear(mm, vmaddr, ptep);` were wrapped in a conditional that executes only when `(pgstev & _PGSTE_GPS_USAGE_MASK) == _PGSTE_GPS_USAGE_UNUSED` or `(pgstev & _PGSTE_GPS_ZERO)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, swapped PTEs are no longer always cleared and have their softleaf entry removed during this helper call. Those operations now happen only for entries whose PGSTE state indicates unused GPS usage or the zero flag, preventing the function from zapping and clearing swap-backed entries that are still considered in use according to the PGSTE metadata.

relevance_review.reason: This change introduces PGSTE state handling directly inside gmap_helper_zap_one_page(), which is the function implicated in the root cause. Even though it only adds a local variable, it is preparatory for validating guest-page state before clearing entries.

The change directly matches the root cause: it adds PGSTE state validation before clearing swapped PTEs and softleaf entries, preventing active or zero-tracked guest pages from being incorrectly zapped and corrupted.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional gate on swap PTE state enters the zap path without any PGSTE guest-page-state validation, which is the core missing check behind the bug.
This removes the softleaf entry unconditionally for swapped PTEs, causing guest-tracked state to be discarded even when PGSTE indicates the page is still in use or zero-tracked.
This clears the swap PTE without checking PGSTE state first, directly embodying the erroneous zapping that can corrupt guest memory.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional enters the zap path for any swap PTE without first validating the PGSTE guest-page state. That missing validation is the root cause that allows active or zero-tracked guest pages to be treated as discardable.
This statement clears the swap PTE once inside the unconditional swap-PTE path, discarding the mapping even when PGSTE state may still mark the guest page as in-use or zero-tracked.
This removes the softleaf entry for the swapped page without PGSTE-state validation, causing guest-tracked state to be lost for pages that should not have been zapped.

This commit message itself states the fix is to clear the page table entry when discarding an address that maps to a swap entry.
